questions.stem:
Statements: M > N, N > O, O > P.
Conclusions: I. M > P    II. N > P
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: C is correct. From M>N>O>P: transitivity gives M>P (I ✓) and N>P (II ✓). Both conclusions follow.

questions.stem:
Statements: A = B, B > C.
Conclusions: I. A > C    II. A = C
Which conclusion follows?
questions.explanation: A is correct. A=B and B>C → A>C. Only I follows. II (A=C) contradicts what we derived.

questions.stem:
Statements: P > Q > R = S.
Conclusions: I. P > S    II. Q > S
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: C is correct. P>Q>R=S → P>S (I ✓) and Q>R=S → Q>S (II ✓). Both follow.

questions.stem:
Statements: J ≥ K, K > L, L ≥ M.
Conclusions: I. J > M    II. K > M
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: C is correct. K>L≥M → K>M (II ✓). J≥K>M → J>M (I ✓). Both follow. The ≥ for J≥K doesn't prevent J>M because K>M is certain.

questions.stem:
Statements: X > Y, Z < Y.
Conclusions: I. X > Z    II. Z < X
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: C is correct. X>Y and Z<Y → X>Y>Z, so X>Z. Both I and II state the same relationship (X>Z and Z<X are identical), and both follow.

questions.stem:
Statements: A ≤ B, B < C, D > C.
Conclusions: I. D > A    II. C > A
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: C is correct. D>C>B≥A → D>A (I ✓) and C>B≥A → C>A (II ✓). Both follow.

questions.stem:
Statements: P > Q = R, R < S, T ≤ S.
Conclusions: I. P > S    II. T > Q
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: D is correct. P>Q=R<S: we know P>R but can't compare P and S (S is larger than R, and P is also larger than R — we don't know which is bigger). I doesn't necessarily follow. T≤S and Q=R<S: Q<S but T≤S, so T could be greater or less than Q. II doesn't necessarily follow.

questions.stem:
Statements: V ≥ W > X, X = Y.
Conclusions: I. V > Y    II. W > Y
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: C is correct. W>X=Y → W>Y (II ✓). V≥W>Y → V>Y (I ✓ — even if V=W, still V>Y since W>Y). Both follow.

questions.stem:
Statements: A ≥ B, B = C, C ≤ D, D < E.
Conclusions: I. E > A    II. E > B    III. A ≥ C
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: C is correct. A≥B=C≤D<E. II: B=C≤D<E → B<E ✓. III: A≥B=C → A≥C ✓. I: A≥C≤D<E — A could be very large (much greater than E), so E>A is NOT necessarily true. Only II and III follow.

questions.stem:
Statements: P < Q = R ≥ S > T.
Conclusions: I. R > T    II. Q ≥ S    III. P < S
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: B is correct. I: R≥S>T → R>T ✓. II: Q=R≥S → Q≥S ✓. III: P<Q=R≥S — since S≤R and P<R, we can't directly compare P and S (S could be smaller than P). III does not necessarily follow.
